anomaly_def.Name: Buffer Cache and Latch Contention Anomaly + CPU Resource Anomaly + Network and Connectivity Resource Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Buffer Cache and Latch Contention Anomaly : Simultaneous hot-page access forces sessions to serialize on buffer-cache latches, page pins, or I/O slots, stalling execution at the storage-engine layer.
CPU Resource Anomaly : Database and ancillary processes drive host CPU utilisation to saturation, exhausting compute cycles and lengthening run-queue and scheduler waits.
Network and Connectivity Resource Anomaly : Client ↔ server transport, listener, socket, or authentication resources become bottlenecked, delaying connection setup and data transfer.

When these three root causes strike together the system exhibits a multilayer bottleneck: 1) intra-engine waits such as buffer-busy and page-latch spikes, 2) host-level symptoms of CPU exhaustion—high load averages, context-switch storms, runaway spin polling in latch code, and 3) external indicators of connectivity stress—rising connection-establishment latency, backlog overflow, and client-side timeouts. Because each tier is impaired, end-to-end response times degrade non-linearly, with seemingly random query slowdowns, erratic throughput, and bursts of failed or abandoned client sessions that mask the true root causes.

Causal interaction: Hotspot pages force sessions into latch spin loops that chew CPU; the inflated CPU demand pushes the host to saturation, lengthening the time threads hold latches and further intensifying buffer contention. The overwhelmed schedulers also delay kernel-space network interrupts and socket processing, which inflates round-trip times and backs up the database listener. Conversely, stalled or retried client connections keep backend processes in a suspended or half-active state while still owning buffer pins, extending the lifetime of page locks and exacerbating latch queues. The feedback loop among latch spin, CPU starvation, and network backlog can cascade quickly, turning localized hot-page contention into cluster-wide performance collapse.

entry.official_definition: Sets the interval between optional checks that the client is still connected while running queries.
entry.trigger_condition: During a long-running query, PostgreSQL polls the socket at this interval and can detect a closed connection sooner.
entry.workload_impact: Long-running queries can be aborted sooner after the kernel reports that the client connection is closed.
entry.default_behavior: Default value is 0, disabling connection checks.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when connection establishment, authentication exchange, or session activity does not progress within the allowed time budget.
entry.solution_guidance: Check connection lifecycle, client responsiveness, authentication latency, idle-session handling, and whether connection pools are holding stale sessions.
